Build only E02 design 3.2/3.4 authentication and roster, the pure 3.3 access truth table, identity-owned parts of 3.1/4/5/6/8/11, and their tests. Leave persisted grants to T2, vault to T3, UI to T4, module registration and real-stack acceptance to T5. No getContext: D16 assigns it to E23. Before starting, require E01's actual kernel.testing, StorageSession/platform, generated effective models, operation-role table and toolchain, and resolved R-E02-5/9/22. Inspect the provider-owned paths from E01 section 13 once they exist. In particular do not invent the return type of require_roles or the missing RosterMember, SessionRevocation, namespace, bootstrap and CLI bindings. Freeze agreed application declarations before T2/T3 start. No new public endpoint, event or role.

Use SessionContext exactly SYSTEM 5.7. Implement the agreed require_roles(operation_id: str), RosterPort.crew(at), members(), person_ids() and session liveness only after R-E02-9 supplies their complete types. Roster extensions in E22/E31 remain requested, never aliases. Table names and constraints are E02 section 5: identity_person, identity_credential, identity_session, identity_adapter_token, identity_device, identity_auth_bucket, identity_access_generation. Use only StorageSession on these tables and expand-only 0001_identity.sql. Every mutation uses the agreed reference-only local ReplicationChange with export_projection=None, never a credential/token/verifier/digest in a replication body. No home-writer designation grants roster export. T5 owns registration of prefixes/settings/audiences, so return the exact agreed declarations and bounds in your handoff rather than edit module.py.

The router implements only POST /v1/sessions createSession (SessionCreate to 201 Session with token once), GET /v1/sessions/current getCurrentSession (Session without token), DELETE /v1/sessions/current deleteCurrentSession (Idempotency-Key, 204), and GET /v1/crew listCrew (CrewMember/page). Copy roles/statuses/headers from the opened OpenAPI, not a role-name list from memory. SessionCreate has crew/station/ground/operator/editor; adapter tokens do not use it. SessionContext has adapter but no acting officer kind. Editor has attributed operator actor. Crew requires person_id; non-person kinds reject it. Use identity_credential for one principal per non-person kind, Argon2id with the exact section 11 bounded descriptors, separate aggregate principal/client/global attempt reservations, a dummy verifier for unknown principals and generation recheck before issuance. Password changes, session termination and audit commit together; do not implement administrative reset or recovery beyond R-E02-16. Old-epoch sessions end before serving, background requests never renew human presence, and flight refuses ground sign-in. Device enrollment/revocation is the DEPLOYMENT 5.2 CLI interim through the agreed E20 binding, never invented device HTTP routes.

Write tests first: test_sessions.py covers T009/010/012/015/019 (R02, durable-session and no-secret invariants); test_routing.py covers pure T001 plus T004/005 (R29/V08/V09/D09 policy), including station rejection before patient validation, all LIVE/REPLAY/SIM partitions, demo_operator only in explicit demo profile and verified-officer manual capture without E05/E26. It cannot claim acquisition integration before T5. test_bounds.py covers T020/021: property tests of IDs, every section 11 identity bound, independent rate limits under rotating IDs/clients and concurrent KDF work, roster mission-day boundaries and nullable fields, and a scratch ui-copy.json error_messages edit through E01's mapper without changing a safety mapping. Read config-ui-copy.schema.json and example, never create config/ui-copy.json. Credential fixtures are explicit test/demo input, not runtime defaults.

Faults: crash/disk-full at attempt reservation, issuance and change commits; audit failure rolls back; retry of ended sign-out remains unauthenticated; in-flight verification loses to credential generation change; clock regression, restart and missing configuration deny safely; no unknown patient inferred from a partial/disagreeing reading; incapacitated/absent subject and ground outage do not disable verified manual-care policy. Positive and adversarial policy expectations both required. Full runtime fallback is T5/T4, not a mock-router pass. Done requires these owned gates and a typed interface handoff for T2/T3/T5; incomplete shared bindings block acceptance rather than introduce permissive stubs.

Only an authenticated subject creates/revokes a grant, with mission/origin, exact object, recipient, purpose, explicit fields/actions, policy, revision and absolute validity. Empty/unknown dimensions deny; revision conflict never merges. The subject may read own data, but an officer/helper/station is not a general chart reader. Accepted tasks need current consent; the limited open help summary uses actual same-subject membership and access audit, never readable_by. Report recipients receive only owner-approved immutable snapshots through their owners, never vault rows. No journal export. No roster/consent recipient export until R-E02-11 catalogue support exists; still declare local reference changes under SYSTEM 5.7.

Creation of finite consent schedules SYSTEM 5.10 AbsoluteDeadline in its UoW. The supplied expiry handler checks revision/generation and commits terminal state, audit, invalidation and completion. ReadSnapshot checks are pure and deny at expiry before sweep. Follow E02 3.1 exactly: no hidden UoW or mutation from allows/AudienceRule. R-E02-21 must publish the atomic clock/startup fence, including sub-tolerance regressions, before positive finite grants are enabled. Correction cannot reactivate them; renewal is a new owner grant ID. Never remove finite expiry or replace it with null to pass a test. Revocation retains audit/history, fences unsent streams using SYSTEM 5.7.1, and rechecks saved-result visibility through SYSTEM 5.8. Revocation or storage errors are not evaluator failures.

Tests first in test_grants.py: T003/007/010/013 (R02/E02-03) plus consent T012/020/021. Exercise property-based field intersection and removal monotonicity; positive narrow grant; wrong purpose/recipient/object/mission/origin; empty, future, expired, revoked and null expiry; same key on another target/parameter conflict; late identical replay with revoked access denies; stale revision and concurrent revoke/action. The c1.3 regression first observes expiry via read-only authorization, holds the sweep, moves time back or restarts, reauthenticates and still denies with no read-side write. Force failure in the clock fence and in audit; neither allows access. test_policy.py covers T001/002/017/018: uninvolved/station/wrong-subject/closed-help denial, subject/opener/helper positive limited panel, names only/no doses, report field-grant positive plus journal denial, acting assignment not a role or chart grant, D10 owner authentication without taking E22 state ownership. Test current schemas/facts only; pending provider facts cannot be invented for integration.

Change a scratch ui-copy.json error_messages label using E01's generated mapper to prove consent content is configuration-driven; no extra consent configuration document. Bounds are consent.active_per_subject_max, consent.fields_max and inherited finite storage/scheduler/identity paging bounds from E02 11. Crash/retry, disk full, uncertain time, delayed grant rows, incapacitated subject, absent providers and long transport outage must preserve the fail-closed and emergency exceptions. Unit fakes are allowed only from fixed ports; T5 owns real HTTP/SSE/sharing acceptance. Done requires every owned gate and exact service declarations for T5; missing expiry/provider integration remains blocking.

Implement exactly PrivateKeyVault.create_entry_key(*, owner_person_id, entry_id), revoke(*, owner_person_id, entry_ids, command_key), revocation(revocation_id), is_revoked(*, entry_id), fingerprint(*, owner_person_id, canonical_identity_and_body), encrypt(*, key_id, plaintext, associated_data), decrypt(session, *, reference, blob, associated_data), with the precise types from SYSTEM 5.8.1. No identity, consent or private database tables are owned by this task. Backend records are exactly those accepted under R-E02-20; do not improvise table names or migrations.

Distinct random DEK and live entry wrapping key per entry/version, fresh nonce, owner/entry/version associated data and per-owner keyed HMAC follow DEPLOYMENT 5.4 and SYSTEM 7.4. Credentials authorize access and never derive erased keys. Every decrypt verifies current session, live hub reference and current vault generation through accepted provider bindings, with no other module's table access. Every allocation/deletion joins E01's all-writer barrier, ordered before hub UoW. The vault never reacquires the barrier or starts a second coordinator. Revoke persists the shared intent, immediately denies unwrap, destroys only the targeted entry wrapping keys, and reports complete only after all registered key-bearing replicas attest. Missing replica stays pending; no silent eviction. Recovery uses E01's intents/scheduler and the current backend, never restored key mirrors.

Fault every seal/hub/receipt and intent/destruction/replica receipt boundary; duplicate retry never creates another entry or false acceptance. Backup A/B, delete A, restore old paired data against current vault: A denied and B still readable. Reject old vault image, absent media after laptop loss, unknown current generation and credential reset as private-owner proof. Concurrent paired backup must block allocation/deletion for journal and report versions; snapshots contain no keys or fingerprint secrets. No plaintext, private hash or sensitive errors in logs.

Bound operations with private.recovery_batch, identity.vault_call_timeout_ms and the accepted finite replica descriptor, respecting E02 11 and SYSTEM 5.11. Sign in owner A, display legitimate private content, then disconnect/hide/suspend/expire/switch to B; prove no private repaint through late response, Back or bfcache. Warm E26's real signed cache, stop the hub/auth/storage/model/devices/link and show fixed help within the charter 500 ms budget; verify the configured printed-card fallback without inventing a screen.
